T: Fish for the dragon, stew for the Vikings.
D: A young Viking who can't fight befriends the dragon he was meant to kill.
P: Serve the fish bites when Hiccup offers Toothless a fish.
S: Panko crumbed white fish strips with a lemon dill yoghurt dip
White fish strips crumbed in panko and fried golden, with lemon and a herby yoghurt dip.
Stoick's skillet bread with honey butter
Stoick the Vast's table in the Great Hall

Crusty seeded bread baked in a blazing hot skillet, torn at the table and slathered with whipped honey and sea salt butter. Mix 500g bread flour, 7g yeast, 10g salt, 2 tbsp mixed seeds and 350ml warm water and knead 8 minutes. Rest 1 hour. Shape into a round and put in an oiled 26cm ovenproof skillet, slash the top, brush with water and scatter more seeds. Rest 30 minutes. Bake at 230C for 30 minutes until it sounds hollow. Beat 125g soft butter with 2 tbsp honey and flaky salt and serve with the warm bread.
Charred smoked sausage chunks with wholegrain mustard
Thick smoked sausages charred over the fire until the skins split, cut into chunks and served with grainy mustard for dipping.
M: Lamb shoulder, carrot, parsnip and pearl barley in beef stock
Lamb shoulder stewed slowly with carrots, parsnips, pearl barley, thyme and stock for two hours until thick and tender.
Toothless lighting up the sky over Berk

Chicken marylands rubbed with smoked paprika, garlic and rosemary, roasted until charred, then lacquered with smoky honey and served with roast carrots. Heat the oven to 200C. Rub 4 chicken marylands with 2 tbsp oil, 2 tsp smoked paprika, 2 crushed garlic cloves, chopped rosemary and salt. Roast on a tray with 6 halved carrots for 40 minutes. Warm 3 tbsp honey with half a tsp smoked paprika and 1 tbsp cider vinegar. Brush over the chicken and roast 10 minutes more until sticky and charred at the edges. Rest 5 minutes and spoon the pan juices over.
W: Soft cinnamon cakes baked in muffin cases and brushed with warm honey
Small honey and spice cakes baked in a muffin tin and glazed with warm honey.
K: Apple juice simmered with berries, cinnamon, star anise and orange

Mixed berries simmered with apple juice, cinnamon, star anise and orange peel, strained and served steaming in mugs with a few whole berries. Put 300g frozen mixed berries, 1L cloudy apple juice, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 star anise, 3 strips of orange peel and 1 tbsp honey in a saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook 10 minutes, pressing the berries. Strain through a sieve into a jug. Pour into 4 mugs and drop in a few fresh blueberries. Serve hot, or chill and pour over ice in summer.

s.note: Panko crumbed white fish strips with a lemon dill yoghurt dip
s.how: Cut 500g white fish fillets into strips. Dip in 50g flour, 2 beaten eggs and 120g panko, and fry at 180C for 3 minutes until golden. Mix 200g Greek yoghurt with lemon and chopped dill and serve with lemon wedges.

s.note: Charred smoked sausage chunks with wholegrain mustard
s.how: Cook 600g thick smoked sausages over high heat for 8 minutes, turning, until charred and split. Cut into chunks and serve on a board with 4 tbsp wholegrain mustard for dipping.

m.note: Lamb shoulder, carrot, parsnip and pearl barley in beef stock
m.how: Brown 1kg diced lamb shoulder, then add 1 onion, 3 carrots and 2 parsnips in chunks, 100g pearl barley, thyme and 1.25L beef stock. Cover and simmer 2 hours until the lamb is tender and the barley is plump. Serve in big bowls with bread.

w.note: Soft cinnamon cakes baked in muffin cases and brushed with warm honey
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 125g honey, add 2 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour, 1 tsp cinnamon and 80ml milk. Spoon into 12 muffin cases and bake at 175C for 18 minutes. Brush with 2 tbsp warm honey while hot.

d.note: Apple juice simmered with berries, cinnamon, star anise and orange
d.how: Put 300g frozen mixed berries, 1L cloudy apple juice, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 star anise, 3 strips of orange peel and 1 tbsp honey in a saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook 10 minutes, pressing the berries. Strain through a sieve into a jug. Pour into 4 mugs and drop in a few fresh blueberries. Serve hot, or chill and pour over ice in summer.
